newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil authorises system to guarantee wheat price.
newsitem.headline: Brazil authorises system to guarantee wheat price.

text.p: The Brazilian government has published a decree authorising a new system to guarantee a minimum price for domestic wheat while relieving the government of the cost of having to carry stocks.

"In face of current market circumstances, it is necesary for the federal government to intervene in the commercialisation of domestic wheat to guarantee official minimum prices," said the decree in the government's official gazette.
But "the high costs of warehousing and looking after the product suggest there should be no public stocks," it added.

The government has therefore devised a system in which millers will compete to buy wheat in electronic auctions which set not the outright price but the level of the subsidy to be paid by the government.
The buyer then pays the government the minimum price of 157 reais ($153.92) minus the subsidy set in the auction while the government pays the farmer the full 157 reais.
Millers anticipate almost all of Brazil's 1996 harvest, estimated at 2.8 million tonnes, will be sold in this way.
Without the system, domestic producers had feared millers would import Argentine wheat which currently is being quoted at $143 a tonne amid a background of falling world prices.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
